title: Add component burn-rate alerts keyed by public status components (paging + runbook links)
author: Aisha Bello
description: Context: As part of the status page transparency upgrades, we need component-level signals that are (a) consistent with our public component taxonomy and (b) actionable for on-call. This PR adds multi-window, multi-burn burn-rate alerts keyed by status component labels (component_id, region, capability) and routes pages to SRE on-call with direct links to the status page update runbook + per-component dashboards. Motivation: Recent incidents showed we were slow to declare partial impact (e.g., Streaming only, or us-east only) because our paging was still too service-oriented (gateway/scheduler) and didn’t map cleanly to the customer-facing component list. These alerts are intended to improve time-to-detection + reduce comms ambiguity by making the component/region impacted explicit from the first page. What’s included: 1) New alert rule groups for the public status components (Hosted API, Streaming, Embeddings, Reranking, Console) with region scoping for us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast where metrics exist today; 2) Standard labels on alerts: component_id, region, capability, severity, and runbook; 3) Pager routing: page SRE on-call for Sev1/Sev0 burn (fast burn), and ticket/notify for slower burns; 4) Runbook links and dashboard annotations embedded into alert annotations, pointing to the status-page update runbook and component health dashboards; 5) Guardrails: basic anti-noise defaults (minimum traffic / request volume gate) to avoid paging on low-QPS components and staging. Thresholds: Uses standard multi-window burn-rate approach; initial defaults are tuned to mirror existing product SLO burn semantics but applied per-component. Fast burn: 5m/1h window, page. Slow burn: 30m/6h window, notify. Notes/assumptions: This PR assumes upstream instrumentation is (or will soon be) labeling request metrics with component_id/region/capability; where labels are missing today, the alert rules are present but disabled behind a feature flag until the observability pack lands. Rollout: Start with Hosted API + Streaming for us-east/us-west enabled; keep other components/regions disabled pending label coverage audit. Validation: Ran rules against last 7d in prod Prometheus; verified we would have paged correctly for the 2025-11-07 us-east streaming degradation without increasing page volume on normal days. Screenshots/links are in the internal thread referenced below.

illustrative_snippet: Example rule (simplified): alert: StatusComponentBurnRateFast expr: (burn_rate_5m{component_id!="", env="prod"} > 14.4) and (burn_rate_1h{component_id!="", env="prod"} > 6) and (requests_5m{env="prod"} > 500) for: 2m labels: severity: "page" team: "sre" component_id: "{{ $labels.component_id }}" region: "{{ $labels.region }}" capability: "{{ $labels.capability }}" annotations: summary: "High error budget burn for {{ $labels.component_id }} ({{ $labels.region }})" runbook: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/.../status-page-update-runbook" dashboard: "https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/..." statuspage_guidance: "If customer impact is confirmed, update the matching public component + region."
review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (SRE) - 2025-11-19: Can we ensure these don’t page when traffic is low (esp. ap-southeast overnight)? Also please confirm the annotation includes component_id/region so comms lead can copy/paste quickly.

Aisha Bello - 2025-11-19: Added request volume gate (requests_5m > 500) and restricted enablement to us-east/us-west initially. Annotations now include component_id + region + capability and direct links to the status page runbook + dashboard.

Allison Grant (Observability) - 2025-11-20: The label names need to match the taxonomy/schema work (component_id, region, capability). Also: can we avoid using internal service names in the alert name/summary?

Aisha Bello - 2025-11-20: Updated to component_id/region/capability everywhere; removed gateway/scheduler references from summaries. Alert names are now StatusComponentBurnRateFast/Slow and the summary is strictly customer-facing component naming.

Christine Wong - 2025-11-20: For the runbook link, please point to the status-page update runbook and add a sentence reminding folks to validate impact before marking degraded. Also: where do we flip enablement flags?

Aisha Bello - 2025-11-20: Done. Flags live in alerts/config/status_components_rollout.yaml; documented in README. Added guidance annotation: 'Validate impact using dashboard link before posting public update.'
Miles Thornton - 2025-11-21: +1. One more request: add a distinct route for 'severity: page' to ensure it hits SRE on-call and doesn’t go to the generic observability channel.
Aisha Bello - 2025-11-21: Added routing policy status_component_paging.yaml mapping severity=page -> PagerDuty service 'sre-oncall' with dedup key including component_id+region.
rollout_notes: Enablement is gated per component/region in alerts/config/status_components_rollout.yaml. Initial default in this PR: enable Hosted API + Streaming for us-east/us-west only; all other components/regions disabled pending label coverage audit. After merge, SRE will flip flags via a follow-up config-only PR once metrics label coverage reaches >95% for that component/region.
release_notes: Internal: Added component/region burn-rate alerts aligned to public status components; pages SRE on-call for fast-burn conditions and includes status page runbook + dashboard links in alert annotations.
